linkedin.hook: Pooled lending risk is an architectural flaw of early smart contract design.
linkedin.copy:
Most lending markets force an unnecessary trade-off between collateral utility and system solvency. Shared pools dilute yield while exposing every participant to contagion from the weakest listed asset. The formal verification of Blend v2 pool architecture and the new b-token specification on Soroban changes this baseline by moving risk management from monolithic contracts to modular account abstractions.

By integrating Blend v2 b-tokens into Vanna SmartAccounts, positions capture yield while maintaining full borrowing utility. Execution updates process with ~320ms Mercury indexer latency, costing a predictable 0.00014 XLM in gas per invocation. Liquidations operate against an isolated 1.10x Health Factor floor, containing liquidation risk to the individual account rather than draining pooled protocol reserves.

Institutional credit infrastructure requires execution certainty over socialized risk. Builders and quant desks can examine the specification and deploy testnet SmartAccount sandboxes directly at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

reddit.hook: Formal verification of Blend v2 b-tokens and why we plugged them into Vanna SmartAccounts
reddit.copy:
The biggest friction point in Soroban credit markets has been capital efficiency inside pooled lending. Once you supply capital to a lending market, those tokens turn into dead weight that sit idle as collateral. Blend v2 addresses this through its formally verified pool architecture and b-token specification, which tokenizes lending claims into composable primitives.

We built Vanna to make those b-tokens fully active inside isolated SmartAccounts.

Instead of holding static debt positions in a shared pool, a user routes collateral through an isolated SmartAccount sandbox. The account mints Blend v2 b-tokens, collects base yield, and uses those same b-tokens as margin for secondary operations. Because Soroban handles state updates deterministically, we achieve ~320ms Mercury indexer latency for off-chain state reads and 0.00014 XLM fixed gas cost per transaction.

Risk parameters are enforced strictly at the contract layer:

1. Solvency is scoped strictly per SmartAccount. A blow-up in one account cannot drain secondary pools.
2. The liquidation threshold triggers when an account touches the 1.10x Health Factor floor, leaving enough buffer for liquidators to clear bad debt without cascading slippage.
3. Positions are settled via atomic cross-contract calls between the SmartAccount, Blend v2 pool contracts, and the underlying Soroban AMMs.

To test this setup yourself, you can deploy a SmartAccount sandbox on Stellar testnet:

Clone the sandbox scripts or run the web interface at test.stellar.vanna.finance. Fund your testnet wallet using Friendbot, invoke the account factory, and deposit testnet USDC to mint b-tokens. From there, you can run margin operations and test liquidation triggers locally.

Disclosure: I work on the core engineering team at Vanna Protocol.
